items.title: Back on his feet after a knee injury
items.coverAlt: Patients waiting in the OPD corridor
body: A 62-year-old farmer from a village near Khajipalem had been living with knee pain for months after a fall, and could no longer walk to his fields without help.

At the orthopaedics OPD he was examined, given an X-ray and started on treatment and physiotherapy exercises, with medicines provided free of charge. After six weeks of follow-up visits he is walking on his own again.
“I did not have to worry about money even once. The doctors explained everything to me in Telugu and treated me like family,” he says.

items.title: A safe pregnancy with regular check-ups
items.coverAlt: Staff attending to patients in the corridor
body: A young mother from Bapatla District came to the obstetrics & gynaecology OPD in her first trimester. Travelling to a private clinic in town every month was beyond her family’s budget.
At Sai Aarogya Hospital she had every antenatal check-up, blood test and scan advice free of cost, and the team helped her plan a safe delivery.
She now brings her healthy baby for growth monitoring at the paediatrics OPD.

items.title: Clear vision again after cataract care
items.coverAlt: A doctor consulting an elderly patient
body: A retired schoolteacher noticed her eyesight getting cloudy and stopped reading the newspaper, something she had done every morning for forty years.
The ophthalmology team diagnosed a cataract, guided her through treatment and checked on her recovery at follow-up visits — all without any charge.
“Now I read to my grandchildren every evening,” she says with a smile.
